A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work on hard-negative contrastive learning and representation collapse. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny-ImageNet experiments, including classification accuracy, losses, and collapse diagnostics.

after.justification: The image experiments remain, alongside original synthetic-data experiments and additional batch-size, hardening-function, and augmentation studies.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the reported loss aggregation from averaging all same-class pairs together to averaging within each anchor and then across anchors. This changes weighting when anchors have different numbers of positives. The general contrastive-learning framework and backbone remain.

E1.justification: CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny-ImageNet were already evaluated in v1, including its appendix. v2 adds a three-class Gaussian synthetic dataset and Gaussian-noise and SimCLR augmentation scenarios that generate positive pairs without labels, substantially extending the earlier class-sampled evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The reported comparator groups remain SCL versus HSCL and UCL versus HUCL. The added SimCLR and polynomial-hardening experiments test variants within these groups. SINCERE is newly discussed theoretically but is not separately benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 introduces batch sizes 64 and 32, polynomial-hardening configurations, and SimCLR-loss versus InfoNCE controls. The main ResNet-50, 256-negative, 400-epoch, batch-512 configuration remains. Its new description of whole-batch negatives in supervised experiments conflicts with Section 3's class-exclusion rule, leaving that reported setting ambiguous.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained initialization, normalization, and hardness analyses, v2 adds batch-size sensitivity, polynomial versus exponential hardening, and augmentation-versus-loss diagnostics in Appendix B.3–B.5. Synthetic representation plots and Table 2 also extend the evidence about when neural collapse occurs or fails.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds synthetic losses and geometries, near-NC initialization metrics, and batch-size, polynomial-hardening, and SimCLR results. For example, Table 2 newly reports an equal-inner-product error of 0.586 for HUCL at beta 30 after near-NC initialization. The original CIFAR100 loss values in Table 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 removes conditional independence of anchor-positive pairs. Theorems 2–3 add explicit disjoint-support and deterministic-label consequences, while Section 4.3 introduces a batched-loss derivation and Appendix A proves augmentation-model compatibility. These are substantive additions beyond relocating the earlier proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution section newly claim SCL/HSCL optimality without class-conditional independence and extend the advertised theoretical applicability to batched optimization. The original risk-domination and neural-collapse optimality claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 describes independent augmentations as compatible with its UCL latent model. v2 explains that independent augmentations need not yield class-conditional independence and identifies additional practical obstacles involving class balance and support overlap. New synthetic and SimCLR interpretations qualify the benefits of hard negatives and explain failures to attain neural collapse.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, synthetic-data and noise-generation parameters, polynomial-hardening settings, and the SimCLR weighting parameter. It also explicitly describes the additional 400 epochs after near-NC initialization. The principal architecture, optimizer, learning-rate, and hardware disclosures were already present.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning relative to Graf and Khosla by distinguishing label use in negative sampling. It newly connects the results to debiased contrastive learning and SINCERE, contrasts independence assumptions, and incorporates work on augmentation overlap and imbalanced neural collapse.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, related work, mathematical framework, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Earlier appendix proofs move into structured theoretical subsections, experiments receive dedicated thematic subsections, and 'equal angle' becomes the more precise 'equal inner-product' terminology.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 1–5 reappear as v2 Figures 3–7, enlarged and reorganized from horizontal panels into vertical layouts. v2 also adds the sampling diagram, synthetic visualization, six supplementary experimental figures, and Table 2. These changes substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves relevance through the relaxed SCL assumption, augmentation experiments, and clearer UCL limitations. However, its newly advertised batching guarantee has a material proof problem: Section 4.3, Equation 27 applies Jensen's inequality using weights 1/n_b that need not sum to one. Thus an important new theoretical contribution is unsupported as written. The substantive benefits and this new rigor concern prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
